summary:

title: Feature: 15 Years Ago, 'Return To Dream Land' Ushered In Kirby's Golden Era
summary:
Kirban legend.

Kirby has always been one of Nintendo's more consistently successful franchises. While the little pink puffball never had anything remotely resembling a 'dark era' like many other Nintendo series, there was a time around the turn of the century where Kirby began to spin his wheelies a bit.

After the 2000 release of Kirby 64: The Crystal Shards, developer HAL Laboratory immediately began work on Kirby’s next big adventure. Glimmers of a mainline Kirby title for the GameCube featuring the return of the helper system from Kirby Super Star with four-player co-op popped up in various circles over the years, including E3 2005, but a full-on game never materialised.

title: Review: Village In The Shade (Switch 2) - A Farm Sim That Plays With Cosy Tropes In Clever Ways
summary:
Tricks of the shade.

The farming-sim genre needed Village in the Shade. The horror-tinged cosy game plays all the right beats to slot seamlessly into the library of farming adventures that seemingly come out every month. In fact, its visuals, mechanics, soundtrack, and overall feel would make it one of the better cosy titles to come out in the past few years. The real genius of comes in how it turns a mirror onto the player and makes us question why we find this simulated peace so enticing.

My expectations were set expertly by the game’s cold open. I saw my custom main character, who I had just spent a good 10 minutes designing, falling down a well and dying in a pool of blood.

title: Shigeru Miyamoto Becomes First Game Dev To Receive Japan's Prestigious Culture Award
summary:
Onward and upward!

Adding to what is surely the most stacked roster of lifetime achievements, Shigeru Miyamoto is set to be awarded the prestigious Order of Culture award next month.

The award, which first began way back in the 1930s, will be given by the Emperor of Japan on the nation's Culture Day (3rd November), and is awarded to those who have gone above and beyond in their contributions to Japan's art, literature, tech or science scenes.

title: Gallery: iam8bit's Sonic Legacy Cartridges Are Stunning, But Are They Worth The Money?
summary:
For a select few, potentially.

When iam8bit announced its Legacy Cartridge Collection for Sonic and Sonic 2 on Sega Genesis a few months back, it's safe to say that most people were taken aback by the price. Available via iam8bit's official store page, each cartridge — complete with authentic case, instruction manual, and poster — is priced at $99.99.

That's a lot. Certainly a hefty chunk more than both games cost together digitally on Switch. Hell, you can pick up Sonic Origins Plus for 20 quid these days. So no, for the Average Joe who just wants to play these games in whichever manner is most convenient, these are probably not worth the money.

summary:
"We would like to sincerely apologize".

Third-party video game giant Capcom has suffered a major data breach recently, exposing the personal information of more than 11.7 million customer "CAPCOM ID" accounts around the world.

The data leak includes emails, client IP addresses used during the last login, and other details such as account creation dates. Apparently, only "43 of the cases" leaked additional details such as birth dates, gender, country/region and nicknames.

title: Review: Steins;Gate Re:Boot (Switch 2) - The Timeless Visual Novel Gets A Fresh Lick Of Paint
summary:
El Psy Kongroo.

Want to know why life in a world without time travel is such a bummer? No matter when you decide to take the plunge or how many other games you play, you can only ever experience Steins;Gate for the first time once.

Even more than 15 years on from its debut, it is no exaggeration to call 5pb and Nitroplus’ quirky little character drama on the intricacies of time travel a touchstone of visual novels as a medium, and the bar by which many of its ilk continue to be measured. It is conceptually fascinating, hilarious, tragic, existentially horrifying, heartwarming, thrilling, and everything in between. It is a story where an anime catgirl at a maid café ponders whether it’s God or us who observe the flow of time, and it has my endless gratitude for that.
